matchup_findings.statement: Florida State's explosive passing offense meets a Pittsburgh defense that allows explosive pass plays (+1.36).
Pittsburgh holds the early-down edge: its offense stays ahead of the chains on 1st and 2nd down against this defense (+0.12) more than Florida State does (-1.51).

Pittsburgh owns the stronger opponent-adjusted sustained-efficiency matchup: Pittsburgh offense vs Florida State defense +0.49, Florida State offense vs Pittsburgh defense -0.81 (success rate, opponent-adjusted: Pittsburgh offense #74 of 138, Florida State defense #83 of 138).
Pittsburgh's sustained-efficiency edge is real but not decisive (1.30, below the 2.0 strong threshold): enough for the trailing side to stay in range.
Pittsburgh's offense has swung widely from game to game relative to its opponents (game-to-game residual variation in the 87th percentile of FBS).
Pittsburgh's leading passer in its last game (Holden Geriner) is not its season leader (Mason Heintschel): season passing numbers may not describe the quarterback who plays.
